front.title: The Graviteron: A Unit for the Weight of Independent Evidence

abstract.t: This document defines the Graviteron, a unit that states how much signed, independent evidence supports or contradicts a claim. A Graviteron reading is the weight of evidence of Turing and Good, expressed in decibans: ten times the base-10 logarithm of the factor by which independent checks change the odds of the claim. The document specifies the computation from operator verdicts and measured operator reliability, eight properties that every conforming implementation must satisfy, a reading format that is never a bare number, and language-neutral test vectors. It does not define a decision rule.
